text:
ConocoPhillips gained 2.67% today, closing at $154.03, building on a 5% rise over the past two weeks. The stock's strength tracks with oil prices holding firm—US crude at $103.37 per barrel and global crude at $123.10—and reflects the company's recent earnings power from refining. News that Qatar is actively mediating U.S.-Iran negotiations reduces the risk of a severe geopolitical shock to Middle Eastern oil supplies, while tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz continues despite tensions, suggesting crude will keep flowing and prices stay supported.

The broader backdrop reinforces this: Trump administration pressure on Big Oil over fuel costs appears to have backfired, with oil majors posting surging refining profits as supply tightened rather than gas prices falling. For a major integrated producer like ConocoPhillips, that combination of steady crude prices and strong downstream refining margins is a genuine earnings tailwind.
